drafter.private_reasoning: Assuming our client is the Seller, the draft’s unqualified financial-statement representation and unlimited indemnity create substantial exposure. Narrow those provisions with customary disclosure, knowledge, materiality, survival, basket, and cap protections without identifying or implying any specific confidential matter. Preserve open commercial points for negotiation rather than inventing terms.
drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: Thank you for the initial draft. We have proposed a seller-side framework for the financial-statement representation and indemnity, including disclosure, knowledge and materiality qualifications and customary limits on indemnification. Please provide the proposed Purchase Price and any agreed allocation or payment mechanics so we can complete that provision. We are happy to discuss the proposed indemnity parameters promptly and keep the transaction moving.

edits.text: 4. REPRESENTATIONS. Except as set forth in the disclosure schedules delivered by Seller at signing, Seller represents that, to Seller’s knowledge, the financial statements provided to Buyer were prepared in accordance with the accounting principles consistently applied by Seller and fairly present, in all material respects, the financial condition of the business as of their stated dates. The foregoing representation is made subject to the qualifications and limitations set forth in this Agreement.
edits.name: Seller

edits.text: 5. INDEMNITY. Subject to the limitations in this Section, Seller shall indemnify Buyer for direct losses finally awarded by a court or agreed in a written settlement, to the extent arising from a breach of Seller’s representations or covenants in this Agreement. Seller shall have no liability to the extent a matter is fairly disclosed in the disclosure schedules or otherwise taken into account in determining the Purchase Price. No claim may be made unless written notice describing it in reasonable detail is given before the applicable representation or covenant expires. Seller’s aggregate liability for all claims under this Agreement shall not exceed [10%] of the Purchase Price, and Seller shall have no liability unless aggregate covered losses exceed [1%] of the Purchase Price, in which case Seller shall be liable only for losses above that amount. The foregoing limits shall not apply to fraud or intentional misrepresentation. Neither party shall be liable for punitive, exemplary, special, or consequential damages, except to the extent payable to a third party under a covered claim. The parties shall include customary provisions addressing defense and settlement of third-party claims.
edits.name: Seller

receiver.message_back: The Purchase Price and any allocation or payment mechanics remain subject to diligence and negotiation; we cannot provide agreed terms at this stage. The proposed indemnity limitations are not acceptable as drafted: please remove the knowledge and materiality qualifications from the financial-statement representation and revise the cap, basket, disclosure and price-adjustment exclusions to preserve meaningful recovery for inaccuracies, with the details to be negotiated.

drafter.private_reasoning: The client’s confidential Pembrook information must not be disclosed. The proposed revisions leave price and allocation mechanics open, while offering a negotiating position on the financial-statement representation and indemnity that responds to opposing counsel’s concerns without conceding uncapped or duplicative recovery.
drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: We have revised the draft to leave the Purchase Price and its mechanics for diligence and negotiation. On the financial-statement representation, we have removed the knowledge qualifier and proposed a materiality scrape for purposes of determining breach and Losses, while retaining the stated materiality standard in the representation itself. For indemnification, we propose a 15% aggregate cap and a 1% tipping basket, with recovery from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded. The revised language also narrows the disclosure and price-adjustment exclusions to amounts fairly disclosed with reasonable detail or actually reflected in the final price, and prevents duplicate recovery. These are proposed terms for discussion, including the remaining claim procedures and limitations.

edits.text: 1. PURCHASE PRICE. The Purchase Price, and any allocation, payment mechanics, or adjustment thereto, remain subject to diligence and further negotiation and shall be set forth in a mutually agreed written amendment or definitive schedule to this Agreement before Closing.
edits.name: Purchase Price

edits.text: 4. REPRESENTATIONS. Except as set forth in the disclosure schedules delivered by Seller at signing, Seller represents that the financial statements provided to Buyer were prepared in accordance with the accounting principles consistently applied by Seller and fairly present, in all material respects, the financial condition of the business as of their stated dates. The foregoing representation is subject to the other qualifications and limitations expressly set forth in this Agreement. For purposes of determining whether a breach of this representation has occurred and the amount of any Losses arising from such breach, any qualification or exception based on materiality or words of similar import shall be disregarded.
edits.name: Representations

edits.text: 5. INDEMNITY. Subject to the limitations in this Section, Seller shall indemnify Buyer for direct losses finally awarded by a court or agreed in a written settlement ("Losses"), to the extent arising from a breach of Seller’s representations or covenants in this Agreement. For purposes of determining whether a breach has occurred and the amount of Losses, any qualification or exception based on materiality or words of similar import in the applicable representation or covenant shall be disregarded, except for the words “in all material respects” in Section 4, which remain part of the standard for determining whether that representation has been breached. Seller shall have no liability to the extent, and only to the extent, that the matter giving rise to the claim was fairly disclosed in the disclosure schedules with reasonable detail sufficient to identify the nature and scope of the matter, or was specifically reflected in the final Purchase Price or a final purchase-price adjustment, in each case without duplication of any recovery or adjustment. No claim may be made unless written notice describing it in reasonable detail is given before the applicable representation or covenant expires. Seller’s aggregate liability for all claims under this Agreement shall not exceed 15% of the Purchase Price. Seller shall have no liability unless aggregate covered Losses exceed 1% of the Purchase Price, in which case Seller shall be liable for all covered Losses from the first dollar. The foregoing limits shall not apply to fraud or intentional misrepresentation. Neither party shall be liable for punitive, exemplary, special, or consequential damages, except to the extent payable to a third party under a covered claim. The parties shall include customary provisions addressing defense and settlement of third-party claims.
edits.name: Indemnity

receiver.message_back: We appreciate the revisions and agree to continue negotiating the Purchase Price separately, but the financial-statement materiality scrape must apply in determining both breach and Losses, and indemnity should cover otherwise recoverable Losses without requiring a final court award. Our counter is a 25% aggregate cap and a 0.5% tipping basket, with customary carve-outs from the cap for fraud and intentional misrepresentation; we also need to resolve claim procedures and survival periods in the next draft.
